extracted.intended_audience: AQA GCSE English Language examiners and teachers marking Paper 1 (8700/1)
extracted.subtask_description: Marking and assessment guidance for AQA GCSE English Language Paper 1 (Explorations in creative reading and writing), covering procedures, AOs (AO1–AO6) and question-specific level descriptors and indicative content for Q1–Q5.

rubrics_metrics.name: General marking procedure (Annotate → Level → Mark)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three-step process examiners must follow when marking a response: Step 1 Annotate the response; Step 2 Determine a level; Step 3 Determine a mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1: Read through the answer and annotate each section using comments from the statement bank to show demonstrated qualities. Step 2: Start at the lowest level and work up to find the level whose descriptors the answer fulfils; use the Indicative Standard exemplars and standardising scripts to judge. Step 3: Fine tune within the chosen level to award a mark — balance strengths and weaknesses; a student only needs to meet a skills descriptor once to be awarded that level. Always refer to standardising scripts throughout marking. An answer with nothing of relevance must be awarded no marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of response marking instructions (Levels 1–4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Level-based assessment across mark-schemes: Levels 4 → 1 labelled by key words (Perceptive/detailed; Clear/relevant; Some/attempts; Simple/limited) and each level contains skills descriptors and an Indicative Standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Levels show progression from simple awareness to perceptive, detailed performance. To reach a level a student must fulfil one or more skills descriptors for that level. The Indicative Standard provides exemplification (not model answers) and is used with standardising scripts. Use the levels as a ladder: confirm whether the answer meets descriptors at each level before moving up. The number of references is not the determinant — quality of comments is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice to examiners (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Five practical rules examiners must follow to ensure fairness and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1. Refer constantly to the mark scheme and standardising scripts. 2. Always credit accurate, relevant and appropriate responses even if not covered by the mark scheme. 3. Use the full range of marks; do not hesitate to give full marks if merited. 4. Consistency is key to accurate and fair marking. 5. If in doubt about mark allocation, consult your Team Leader.

rubrics_metrics.name: AO1: Identify and interpret information
rubrics_metrics.description: AO1 requires identification and interpretation of explicit and implicit information and ideas, and selection and synthesis of evidence from texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit responses that identify and interpret meaning, draw appropriate inferences, and select/synthesise textual evidence. AO1 is assessed in Section A of the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: AO2: Analyse language and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: AO2 requires explanation, comment and analysis of how writers use language and structure to achieve effects and influence readers, using relevant subject terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AO2 applies to both language (words/phrases/features/techniques/sentence forms) and structure (whole-text, paragraph, and sentence-level features when they contribute to overall structure). Select judicious textual detail, analyse effects of choices, and use accurate subject terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: AO3: Compare ideas and perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: AO3 requires comparing writers' ideas and perspectives and how they are conveyed across two or more texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess candidates' ability to compare content and methods across texts; AO3 is not applicable to every question on this paper (marked as N/A for some questions).

rubrics_metrics.name: AO4: Evaluate texts critically with references
rubrics_metrics.description: AO4 requires critical evaluation of texts supported by appropriate textual references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop convincing critical responses that show understanding of writers' methods, select judicious references and evaluate effects on the reader. Explicit or implicit reference to agreement/disagreement is acceptable. Use level descriptors (16–20, 11–15, 6–10, 1–5 marks) to grade.

rubrics_metrics.name: AO5: Content and organisation for writing
rubrics_metrics.description: AO5 assesses communication (clarity, effectiveness, imagination), selection/adaptation of tone, style and register for forms/purposes/audiences, and organisation of ideas using structural and grammatical features for coherence/cohesion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark writing on content and organisation across four levels with detailed descriptors (Level 4: compelling/convincing communication with extensive vocabulary and inventive structure; Level 3: consistent clear communication; Level 2: some successful communication; Level 1: simple limited communication). For Level 4 the scheme distinguishes Upper/Lower splits (e.g., Upper Level 4 = 22–24 for AO5).

rubrics_metrics.name: AO6: Technical accuracy (20% requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: AO6 requires use of a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate spelling and punctuation; this requirement constitutes 20% of the marks for the specification as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark technical accuracy across four levels (Level 4: sentence demarcation consistently secure, wide punctuation range, full range of sentence forms, consistent Standard English and high-accuracy spelling; Level 3/2/1 decline in control and accuracy). Use AO6 descriptors to award 13–16, 9–12, 5–8, 1–4 marks respectively, and Level 0 where spelling/punctuation prevent understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment mapping (which AOs assessed where)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table mapping Assessment Objectives to Section A and Section B of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section A assesses AO1, AO2, N/A for AO3 (depending on question), and AO4; Section B assesses AO5 and AO6. Use the mapping to apply appropriate AOs to each question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q1: 'List four things' marking rubric
rubrics_metrics.description: Q1 requires students to 'List four things about Master' drawn from lines 1–4. Award 1 mark for each valid point (total 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules: Responses must be drawn only from lines 1–4; responses must relate to 'Master'; responses must show some evidence of selection; responses can be quotations or paraphrase; responses can be a single word; full sentences not required. Indicative content lists acceptable points (e.g., He is academic; He reads; He has travelled; He eats meat every day; He is a little odd; He is nice/decen t) and a list of rejects (e.g., 'He is weird', 'He is rude/unwelcoming', 'He likes travelling' — reject if not verifiable in lines 1–4). Examiner should ask: does it tell you something about Master? Is it from the correct section? Is it accurate? If the response fits 'Master is...' or 'Master has...' does it make sense?

rubrics_metrics.name: Q2: Language analysis (AO2) levels and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Q2 asks 'How does the writer use language here to describe Ugwu's impression of the city?' and assesses AO2 (words/phrases/features/techniques/sentence forms) for 8 marks with Level 4–1 banding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level descriptors: Level 4 (7–8 marks) 'Perceptive, detailed analysis' — analyses effects of writer's language choices, selects a range of judicious textual detail, makes sophisticated/accurate use of subject terminology. Level 3 (5–6) 'Clear, relevant explanation' — explains effects, selects relevant detail, uses terminology. Level 2 (3–4) 'Some understanding' — attempts comment, some textual detail, some terminology. Level 1 (1–2) 'Simple, limited comment' — simple awareness and simple references. Indicative language content includes examples and devices (e.g., metaphor 'too choked with expectation', repetition, alliteration, sibilance, hyperbole, simile, sensory imagery). Note: If a student writes only about language outside the given lines, place the response in Level 1 or 2 according to quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q3: Structure analysis (AO2) levels and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Q3 asks 'How has the writer structured the text to interest you as a reader?' (whole-text/paragraph/sentence-level structural features) for 8 marks, assessed via AO2 structure criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level descriptors mirror Q2: Level 4 (7–8 marks) 'Perceptive, detailed analysis' — analyses effects of structural features, selects judicious examples, uses sophisticated terminology. Level 3 (5–6), Level 2 (3–4), Level 1 (1–2) follow similar stepped expectations. Indicative structural features include: journey structure (chronological movement through time/space), flashback, pivotal doorstep moment, juxtaposition (walls of house vs hut), sustained perspective of main character, delayed introduction of Master, changes in pace (speed up then slow), rises in action towards meeting, focus shifts from outside to inside, and cliff-hanger final sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q4: Evaluation (AO4) levels and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Q4 is an evaluative essay responding to a statement (e.g., extent of agreement with portrayal of Ugwu's feelings) for 20 marks, assessed by AO4 descriptors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level 4 (16–20 marks) 'Perceptive, detailed evaluation' — develops convincing critical response, shows perceptive understanding of methods, selects judicious textual detail, evaluates effects on reader in detail. Level 3 (11–15), Level 2 (6–10), Level 1 (1–5) follow a descending scale. Indicative evaluative content includes points such as: slow-paced garden description as paradise; evocative car description as anticipation; robotic dialogue showing break from past; 'brief moment' as transition; contrast of cement vs mud walls for homesickness; white curtain as rite of passage; listing of furniture emphasises unfamiliarity; delayed introduction may be anti-climactic; final sentence indicates isolation/waiting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q5: Creative writing task — AO5 Content & Organisation (24 marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Q5 creative writing is marked for content and organisation (AO5) with 24 marks available across Levels 4–1, and includes Upper/Lower splits at higher bands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level 4 (19–24) 'Compelling, Convincing Communication' — Upper Level 4 (22–24): communication is convincing and compelling, assured tone/style/register, extensive and ambitious vocabulary, sustained crafting of linguistic devices; organisation: varied/inventive structural features, compelling writing, fluently linked paragraphs. Lower Level 4 (19–21): similar but slightly less extensive. Level 3 (13–18) 'Consistent, Clear Communication' — Upper (16–18) & Lower (13–15) splits with descriptors about vocabulary, structure and engagement. Level 2 (7–12) 'Some successful communication' — upper/lower splits with partial success in tone/structure. Level 1 (1–6) 'Simple, Limited Communication' — simple vocabulary, simple structural features, limited coherence. Level 0: no meaningful writing to assess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q5: Creative writing task — AO6 Technical Accuracy (16 marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Q5 also awards 16 marks for technical accuracy (AO6) following level descriptors for spelling, punctuation, grammar and sentence control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level 4 (13–16): sentence demarcation consistently secure and accurate, wide punctuation used accurately, full range of sentence forms for effect, consistent Standard English with secure control of complex grammar, high accuracy in spelling including ambitious vocabulary. Level 3 (9–12): mostly secure demarcation and punctuation, variety of sentence forms, mostly controlled grammar. Level 2 (5–8): generally accurate spelling including complex words, some control of punctuation, attempts variety of sentence forms. Level 1 (1–4): occasional sentence demarcation, simple range of sentence forms, accurate basic spelling. Level 0: spelling/punctuation so poor that meaning is prevented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q5: Task-specific mark split and instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Q5 creative writing has a split of 24 marks for content & organisation (AO5) and 16 marks for technical accuracy (AO6), totaling 40 marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students may choose between 'Describe a place at sunset' or 'Write a story about a new beginning'. Examiners must apply AO5 and AO6 rubrics separately and combine marks. Apply the level descriptors to allocate marks within bands, using standardising scripts and exemplar responses to calibrate.
